title: US Air Force Cloud One breach, Nov 2026

subject.name: Cloud One
subject.about: Cloud One is the US Air Force's main cloud computing platform, launched in 2017. It lets Air Force and Space Force units run applications for personnel, pay, logistics and maintenance on Amazon, Microsoft, Google and Oracle clouds.

disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by the US Air Force, the Department of Defense, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: A reported breach of a military platform that hosts Air Force personnel, pay and logistics systems, a matter for the national government. The known impact is disruption to parts of the platform; what was reached or taken is not known.
who_is_affected: Air Force and Space Force units and staff whose applications run on Cloud One, where some updates and administrator access have reportedly been held back. Nobody has said personal data was taken, and members of the public need do nothing.

known.text: The Air Force says it does not comment on the security of specific systems, and has neither confirmed nor denied a breach.
Cloud One, launched in 2017, hosts Air Force systems for personnel, pay, logistics and maintenance.

not_known.text: What the hackers reached, and whether any data was taken.
